items: List and differentiate the 7R cloud migration strategies.
Choose an appropriate 7R strategy for a given workload.
Explain the Strangler Fig pattern for incremental migration.
Recognize trade-offs between speed (rehost) and long-term value (refactor).
7R — seven common migration approaches: rehost, replatform, refactor, repurchase, retire, retain, relocate.
Rehost (lift-and-shift) — move as-is with minimal change.
Replatform — move with some optimization, no architecture change.
Refactor/Re-architect — redesign to leverage cloud-native features.
Repurchase — replace with a SaaS product.
Retire / Retain — decommission or keep (for now).
Relocate — move hypervisor/VMware workloads wholesale to the cloud.
Strangler Fig — incrementally replace legacy functionality behind a facade until the old system is "strangled".

blocks.text: Cloud migration is rarely one-size-fits-all. The 7R framework helps an SA map each workload:

items: Rehost ("lift-and-shift"): move VMs as-is. Fast, low risk, but you inherit inefficiencies.
Replatform: move with a few tweaks (e.g., managed database) without re-architecting.
Refactor / Re-architect: redesign to use cloud-native services (containers, serverless, managed data stores) for elasticity and cost savings — highest effort, highest long-term value.
Repurchase: drop custom software for a SaaS equivalent (e.g., CRM).
Retire: shut down redundant systems discovered during discovery.
Retain: keep some workloads on-prem (compliance, latency, cost).
Relocate: move an entire VMware/hypervisor estate to a cloud equivalent with little change.

blocks.text: The SA weighs time-to-value, cost, risk, and business case. Rehost gets you to the cloud quickly; refactor unlocks cloud benefits but needs investment. Retire and retain require honest portfolio analysis.

Big-bang migrations are risky. The Strangler Fig pattern wraps the legacy system with a facade and incrementally routes specific features to new cloud-native implementations. Over time, the new system "strangles" the old one, which can then be retired. This reduces risk, allows continuous delivery, and gives business value early.
